Stargardt disease

A single-arm study reported improved visual acuity, microperimetry, and pattern electroretinography after one year of 650 nm treatment. Disease modification has not been demonstrated.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

A single-arm study reported improved visual acuity, microperimetry, and pattern electroretinography after one year of 650 nm treatment. Disease modification has not been demonstrated.

Summary of the Evidence

One prospective human publication is listed for Stargardt disease. It enrolled 45 patients with stage 1 disease, representing 90 eyes, and followed them through one year of treatment. The source category contains no control group, independent replication, animal model, or laboratory study. Scalinci et al. 2022

Human and clinical evidence

Participants received 650 nm LED treatment for ten minutes twice daily, five days per week, for twelve months. The authors reported statistically significant improvement in best-corrected visual acuity, pattern electroretinography amplitude, and microperimetry from baseline. The design was open-label and single-arm. Without sham or untreated comparison, the results cannot separate treatment effects from test-retest variation, expectation, regression to the mean, or changes in patient performance. The report does not establish slowed progression of Stargardt disease or persistence after treatment stops.

Animal evidence

No Stargardt-specific animal PBM report was listed in the exact category.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No Stargardt-specific in-vitro or ex-vivo report was identified in this category.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The study used a 10 Hz, 650 nm LED for ten minutes twice daily, five days each week, for a year. Its participants had stage 1 disease and were recruited at one center. The results do not establish an effective dose for other stages, other devices, or different schedules.

Interpretation

A single-arm cohort reported improved visual acuity, microperimetry and pattern electroretinography after 12 months. Because it lacked a control group and independent replication, the observed changes cannot establish efficacy or slowed disease progression. A masked controlled study with longer follow-up, reproducible functional outcomes, and retinal structural measures is needed.

Evidence strength in source summaryVisual acuity, microperimetry, and PERG: One uncontrolled signal Disease modification: Not established
Publications and records1 publication: 1 prospective single-arm human study with 45 patients and 90 eyes.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

One prospective single-arm study of 45 patients reported improvement in visual acuity, microperimetry, and pattern electroretinography after 12 months. Without a control group or independent replication, the changes cannot establish treatment efficacy or slowed disease progression. The cohort was selected from one center.

Publication and study types

  • The eyes belong to the same patient cohort and should not be counted as independent participants.
  • There is no control group, independent replication, animal study, or in-vitro publication in the mapped category.
